name: LFM3-1.7B

lineage.how_derived: mid-training (final 3.5T tokens, agentic traces, 256K context), SFT on 1.75T tokens, mixed RL, multi-domain on-policy distillation from six specialist teachers, agentic RL

purpose: A text model for local agents and specialized applications: tool calling, structured outputs, agent harnesses (Hermes Agent, Pi, OpenClaw) and quick single-GPU fine-tuning. The builder says it is not recommended for agentic coding or complex multi-step reasoning because of its size, and knowledge-heavy tasks should use retrieval or search.

license.notes: LICENSE of the repository is byte-identical to the LFM2.5-24B-A2B one (compared 2026-11-19, text read there): Apache-2.0-style grant, but commercial use only while the legal entity stays below 10 million USD annual revenue; non-profits exempt for non-commercial or research use. Verdict policy (README, 2026-11-19): this licence term does not lower tona_fit; kept here for an installer label.

architecture.kind: tri-hybrid dense: gated short convolution + sliding-window attention + global attention
architecture.attention: 13 gated short convolutions (kernel 7), 5 sliding-window attention (window 256), 6 global attention (16 Q / 4 KV heads, partial RoPE 0.5); head-wise sigmoid gate, sandwich norm
architecture.drafter: separate DSpark drafter (LFM3-1.7B-DSpark, up to 3.1x per a HF discussion post by the vendor; not opened)
architecture.why_this_design: Blog: agentic use needs more capability per parameter and fast inference over long context; head-wise gating suppresses activation outliers that hurt quantization and aids stability; partial RoPE lets low-frequency dimensions match on content regardless of distance; SWA gave the best quality-speed trade-off when swapped in for some convolutions; the mix came from an automated hardware-in-the-loop search over 14 device and backend combinations.

variants.notes: also FP8, NVFP4, MLX-4bit, ONNX, OpenVINO repos

mac-64gb+.notes: full 128K context needs about 1.6 GB KV cache (vendor)

engine_support.notes: Official GGUF listed for llama.cpp; Tona has no lfm3 backend.

benchmarks.name: Mac agent test, 65 tasks, success
benchmarks.variant: run by MacPaw, quoted by Liquid AI

strengths: Tool calling and instruction following for its size (vendor)
Very small: 1.1 GB at Q4_K_M, small KV cache (1.6 GB at 128K, vendor)
Low hallucination rate on AA-Omniscience (non-hallucination 92.9, vendor)
Easy to fine-tune (single GPU); a base model is published
weaknesses: Weak on coding by the builder's own statement
Knowledge and long-context retrieval behind Qwen3.5 4B/9B (GPQA 63, RULER 128K 65.6)
soft.behavior: Recommended sampling temperature 0.1, top_k 50, repetition penalty 1.1 for general use; temperature 1.0 top_p 0.95 top_k 20 for math and STEM. ChatML-like template with thinking.
best_for: small local agent worker, router, tool-call or extraction step

user_reports.summary: C23 request answered as C++23 and then written in Python; reply: it is not a coding model, training favours tool calling
A community author fine-tuned five role-specialist 1.7B models from the base for a local multi-agent harness

soft.maturity: Fast-moving vendor; 400k downloads of the GGUF repo in about 4 weeks; family spans text, vision, audio, omni and decision models.

tona_fit.reason: Too small for Tona's coding-agent target (the builder excludes agentic coding), but a strong tiny tool-calling or router model that could run next to a larger model.
